changed_in.5.2: The list of search functions is called `package.searchers`; before this it was `package.loaders`. A searcher now hands back an extra value alongside the loader it found, and that value reaches the loader as a second argument after the module name. The record of what has been loaded is also written later than it was: earlier versions marked a module as being loaded before running it rather than after, so a load that failed part way through made later calls naming that module fail too, and a module that reached back to `require()` for itself while still running was stopped rather than run a second time. The C searcher also changed which end of a versioned module name it keeps: it builds the opening function's name from the part before the first hyphen, so `parcels.rates-v2` looks for `luaopen_parcels_rates`, where earlier versions kept the part after it and looked for `luaopen_v2`. Where the library holds no function under the new-style name, the older one is tried as well.
changed_in.5.4: A second result comes back alongside the module's value — the loader data the searcher supplied, which for the searchers that read from disk is the path the module was found at. Nothing arrives there when the call found the module already loaded and did no loading of its own, which is how a caller tells the two cases apart. The `package.preload` searcher, which had supplied no such value at all, now supplies the string `":preload:"`.
